column2: Yama said to me, "You are not dead, gentle one; the ascetic said to you 'See Yama' with his father's word, blazing like fire; that cannot be made untrue, brahmana.
I am pleased with you; go back, dear one; your father, maker of your body, grieves. I give you whatever is your mind's wish; choose your desires, loving of guests."
Thus addressed by him I replied: "I have come to your domain, hard to turn back from; I wish to see the prosperous worlds of the doers of merit, if I deserve a boon from you."
Mounting me on a vehicle yoked with horses, shining and radiant, the god then showed me all the worlds of the doers of merit, lord of the twice-born.
There I saw splendid dwellings of the self-purified, of various shapes and forms, made wholly of jewels,
white like the moon's disc, with nets of little bells, with many hundreds of floors, with water and groves inside,
shining like beryl and sun, made of silver and gold, the colour of the young sun, standing and moving,
mountains made of food and drink, garments, beds, and trees bearing fruits of all desires standing at the houses,
rivers, lanes, halls, ponds and long lakes on all sides, and sounding vehicles harnessed by the thousand.
Rivers flowing with milk, mountains, and ghee and clear water too; and many regions approved by Vaivasvata I saw, never seen before.
Seeing all that, I said to the King of Dharma, the mighty ancient: "These rivers of milk and ghee, with eternal flow: for whom are they ordained to enjoy?"
Yama said: "Know that you are to enjoy them, who are the givers of cow-products, the good; the other worlds, eternal and free of sorrow, are crowded with those devoted to the gift of cows.
Not the mere gift of them is praised; the vessel, the time, the special cow and the rule are to be known; brahmana, the difference among cows is hard to know, like fire and sun.
A brahmana rich in study, exceedingly ascetic, keeping the sacrificial fires is their worthy vessel; cows released from hardship and come for nourishment: by these doors special cows are praised.

Cows satisfied, after fasting three nights on the ground with only water, are to be given to the satisfied; pleased with calves, with good offspring and attendants, after giving, one should live on cow-products for three days.
Giving a cow of good vows, with bronze milk-pail, with a fine calf and not fleeing, for as many years as she has hairs he enjoys the world of heaven.
So too, giving a self-controlled, strong, vigorous, young ox fit for the yoke to a brahmana, supporting the family, mighty and large, he enjoys worlds measured by the giver of a cow.

One patient with cows, a refuge of cows, grateful, afflicted in livelihood: such they call a worthy vessel; in distress of livelihood, in rush, for great purpose, for farming, for offerings, for childbirth,
for the teacher's sake or the nourishment of a child, cows may be given; the time and place are not special; those born within, well bought, got by knowledge, bought with life, won, and from water.
[Nachiketas said:] Hearing Vaivasvata's word, I asked again: "How does one who has no cow go to the worlds of the givers of cows?"
Then the wise Yama said: "The highest goal is in the gift of cows; but there are givers of cow-substitutes without a cow.
When no cows are had, one who gives a ghee cow, of controlled vow: for him these cows flow with ghee, like loving ones.
When no ghee is had, one who gives a sesame cow, of controlled vow, is carried across hardship by the cow and rejoices in the river of milk.
When no sesame is had, one who gives a water cow, of controlled vow, enjoys this cool river that bears desires."
Such things the King of Dharma showed me there, and seeing them I gained supreme joy, Achyuta.

And I tell you what is dear: a great sacrifice of little wealth has come to me, dear father, born from me; it will proceed by the rule of the Veda.
mahabharata:13:70.43	This curse has been received by me for your favour, since in it I saw Yama; seeing there the great reward of giving, I shall without doubt practise the dharmas of giving.
mahabharata:13:70.44	And the King of Dharma, again and again glad, said this to me, brahmana sage: 'Dear one, be always restrained in giving, and especially give cows.
mahabharata:13:70.45	Pure wealth is not to be scorned by one's own dharma; it is to be given to a vessel suited to place and time; therefore cows are to be constantly given by you; let there be no doubt in you on this.'
mahabharata:13:70.46	These were given in earlier times always by the peaceful-souled, set on the path of giving, not fearing fierce austerities; they gave gifts according to their power.
mahabharata:13:70.47	In due time, as able, leaving envy, pure-souled, faithful, of meritorious conduct, having given and practised austerity, they reached that world and shine in heaven, of meritorious conduct.
mahabharata:13:70.48	This gift won justly is to be given to the twice-born, given to a vessel after examining; for ten days one should live on cow-products, milk, dung or cow's urine.
mahabharata:13:70.49	The giver of a bull would be one with the Vedic vow; the gift of a pair of oxen is the gaining of the Veda; the gift of one yoked to cows is the gaining of a sacred ford; the gift of a tawny cow is the release of sin.
mahabharata:13:70.50	Giving even one tawny cow in a proper way, he is freed from stain; there is nothing higher than the juice of cows; they call the gift of cows very great.
mahabharata:13:70.51	Cows, flowing, support the worlds, and cows produce food in the world; one who knows that and does not come to the kindness of cows is a sinful-minded goer to hell.
mahabharata:13:70.52	Whether you are to give a thousand cows, a hundred, fifty or ten, with good calves, or even one to a good brahmana: she will be a river of holy fords there.
mahabharata:13:70.53	By attainment, nourishment and protecting the world, cows are equal on earth to the sun's rays; one is the word, offspring and enjoyment; therefore the giver of a cow shines like the sun.
mahabharata:13:70.54	A pupil should choose his teacher in the gift of cows; he is the speaker, constantly the giver of heaven; this is a very great dharma of those who know rules, for rules rely on the first rule.
mahabharata:13:70.55	This gift won justly is to be given to the twice-born; having given to a vessel, you should cause to obtain after examining; immortals and men hope in you, and we too, on being born, are of meritorious conduct.
Thus addressed by the King of Dharma, great sage, bowing my head to the righteous-souled one, permitted by that Vaivasvata, I came back to the root of the blessed one's feet.
[Yudhishthira said:] And how the great-souled Nriga suffered sorrow from one offence done through ignorance, grandfather, greatly wise one,
and how, when Dvaravati was being settled, Krishna became the cause of his release when he was lifted up: that too I have grasped.
But I have a doubt about the world of cows, lord; I wish to hear truly where givers of cows enter.
[Bhishma said:] On this too they recite this ancient Itihasa, as Shatakratu asked the lotus-born this very thing.
[Shakra said:] "Overcoming the splendour of the dwellers of heaven with your own brightness, I see those who dwell in the world of cows going; here I have a doubt.
What are the worlds of cows like, blessed one? Tell me, sinless one; those that givers live in; I wish to know this.
What kind, what fruit, and what is highest in their quality there? And how do people go there, free of fever?
For how long does the giver enjoy the fruit of giving? How is a gift many-fold, or how even small?
And how can the giver of much be equal to a giver of little, lord, and how can a giver of little be a giver of much, lord?
And what kind of fee is distinguished in the gift of cows? You ought to tell me this truly, blessed one."
[Brahma said:] There are worlds of many kinds, Shakra, that you do not see; I see them, and the women who are one-husband wives.
By very good deeds too, the sages of good vows, brahmanas of good conduct, go to them with their bodies.
By giving up the body and by a pure mind, those of good vows see even here those worlds as in a dream.
Thousand-eyed, hear of what qualities those worlds are: Time does not run there, nor old age nor sin; nor is anything else inauspicious, nor disease nor weariness there.
Whatever the cows wish in mind there, Vasava, they get all that by my direct sight; going at will, moving at will, they enjoy desires from desire.
Ponds, lakes, rivers, various forests, houses, mountains and whatever wealth there is,
whatever is pleasing to all beings is seen there; know those worlds to be so; there is no world higher than that.
There, Shakra, go the best of men who are all-enduring, patient, loving, devoted to teachers, free of egoism.
A man gentle, self-controlled, devoted to the gods, host of all, and compassionate, of such qualities goes to the eternal and imperishable world of cows.
An adulterer does not see this world, nor a killer of his teacher, nor a liar, nor a brahmana always slandering, calm in the Veda, nor one evil-souled and joined with other faults.
Neither a betrayer of friends, nor a cheat, nor an ingrate, nor a crafty, crooked hater of dharma, nor a killer of a brahmana would even in mind see the world of cows, the abode of the meritorious.
All this has been told to you skilfully, lord of gods; now hear, Shatakratu, the fruit of those devoted to the gift of cows.
One who gives cows bought with wealth gained by inheritance gains imperishable worlds bought with wealth earned by dharma.
One who, having won wealth at dice, buys cows and gives them gains, Shakra, the fruit of a divine ten thousand years.
Cows that are one's inheritance, earned by just means, when given, become imperishable and fixed for the givers.
And one who, having received cows, gives them with a very pure mind: know, lord of Shachi, that he too has imperishable fixed worlds here.
One who speaks truth from birth, of controlled senses, patient with the stings of twice-born, has a goal equal to that of cows.
A brahmana should never be told what should not be told, lord of Shachi; he should not harm cows in mind, living by cows and kind to cows.
Hear the fruit, Shakra, for one devoted to truth and dharma: a cow equal to a thousand cows is his.
Hear the fruit for a kshatriya joined with these qualities: for him too a cow equal to a hundred is certain.
If a vaishya has these qualities, fifty; and for a trained shudra a quarter of the fruit is remembered.
One who practises this, joined with truth, serving the teacher, self-controlled, patient, a worshipper of gods, calm, pure, wise, of dharmic character and not boastful,
gains great fruit, having given a milch cow to a twice-born by this rule; he should always give, eating once a day, steady in truth and serving his teacher.
One who studies the Veda, is devoted to cows, always welcomes cows on seeing them, and bows to cows from birth: hear his fruit, Shakra.
The fruit that would be from sacrificing with the Rajasuya, or from sacrificing with much gold, they say his fruit is equal to that, the foremost; all good sages and perfected ones say so.
One who, always keeping the cow vow, truthful, calm, wise, gives something to the cows first, before the devoted eat, would gain in a year the merit of a thousand cows, of meritorious conduct.
One who eats one meal and gives one to the cows, keeping the cow vow, kind to cows, for ten endless years.
One who, buying a cow with one meal, gives her: for as many days as were told, Shatakratu, for that many hundreds of cows he gains eternal fruit.
This is the fruit for a brahmana; hear what is said for a kshatriya: five years is remembered as the kshatriya's fruit, half of that for a vaishya, and for a shudra half of a vaishya.
One who, having sold himself, buys cows and gives them, gains fruit for as many cows as he touches; for each hair, greatly fortunate one, his worlds are imperishable.
One who gives cows won in battles: know, Kaushika, those are eternal, equal to selling oneself.
When no cows are had, one who gives a sesame cow, of controlled vow, is carried across hardship by the cow and rejoices in the river of milk.
Not the mere gift of them is praised; the vessel, time, special cow and rule matter; the knowledge of time, brahmana, and difference among cows are hard to know, like fire and sun.
One rich in study, of pure birth, calm, keeping the fires, afraid of sin, grateful, patient with cows, not over-sharp, a refuge, afflicted in livelihood: such they call a worthy vessel.
In distress of livelihood and very sunk, for farming, for offerings, in childbirth, for a teacher or for the growth of a child, one may give a cow at a special place and time.
Those born within, well bought, got by knowledge, bought with life, won, and from the family, released from hardship and come for nourishment: by these doors special cows are praised.
All are praised that are strong, rich in conduct and age, and fragrant; as the Ganga is the best of rivers, so the tawny is the best of the white cows.

Cows satisfied, after fasting three nights on the ground with only water, are to be given to the satisfied, with well-fed calves that drink milk and graze well; after giving, for three days one should live on cow-products.
Giving a cow of good vows, with a fine calf, of auspicious conduct, not fleeing, for as many years as she has hairs he lives in the next world.
So too, giving to a brahmana a young, strong, trained ox fit for the yoke, bearing the plough, of endless strength, he gains ten worlds of the giver of a cow.
One who protects brahmanas and cows in a wilderness, Kaushika, and is freed with safety: hear the fruit of his merit; it is eternal, equal to the fruit of the horse sacrifice.
At the time of death, thousand-eyed, whatever livelihood he desires, the many divine worlds, or whatever is in his heart,
he gains all that by that deed; permitted by cows, he is honoured everywhere.
But one who follows a cow in forests by this rule, eating grass, dung and leaves, free of longing, restrained and pure,
he must live without desire, glad, Shatakratu, in my world with the gods, or in whatever world he wishes.
[Brahma said:] Those who steal cows for food or sale, or to give to a brahmana: hear the fruit of that.
One who for sale, unrestrained, kills or eats, and those wishing it who approve a man who kills,
the killer, the eater, and one who approves sinks for as many years as the cow has hairs.
Whatever faults and of what kind there are in one who injures a twice-born's sacrifice, in selling and in theft, those faults are remembered, lord.
One who, having stolen a cow, gives it to a brahmana, goes to hell for as long as the fruit of the gift.
Gold is called the fee for the gift of cows, greatly radiant one; gold is said to be the highest for a fee, without doubt.
The gift of a cow carries across seven ancestors before and after; having given gold as a fee, it is said to be twofold.
Gold is the highest gift, gold the highest fee; gold is a purifier, Shakra, remembered as the highest of purifiers.
Raghava also told it to his dear brother, the glorious Lakshmana, and Lakshmana told it to the sages while living in the forest, lord.
This came down by tradition; sages of sharp vows and righteous kings bore it, hard to bear; it was told by my teacher to me, Yudhishthira.
The brahmana who always recites this in a brahmanical assembly, at sacrifices, at gifts of cows, and in a meeting of two,
his worlds are said to be imperishable, with the gods always: so said the blessed Brahma, the Supreme Lord.
[Yudhishthira said:] What fruit is told of vows, and of what kind, greatly radiant one? What is the fruit of restraints, and what of good study?
What is the fruit of self-control, and of bearing the Vedas, and what of teaching? I wish to know all.
What fruit, grandfather, in the world for one who does not accept gifts? What fruit is seen for him who gives what is heard?
What fruit for heroes devoted to their own work? What is told of truth, and what of celibacy?
What of serving father and mother, serving the teacher and instructor, of compassion and kindness?
I wish to know all this, grandfather, exactly and without remainder, knower of dharma; my curiosity is great.
[Bhishma said:] One who takes up a vow as laid down, unbroken and rightly begun, has eternal worlds.
The fruit of restraints, king, is seen here directly; this fruit of restraints and sacrifices has been gained by you.
By gifts and various sacrifices, as the self-controlled are joined with forgiveness: a giver gets angry, a self-controlled man does not; therefore self-control is above giving.
One who gives without anger has eternal worlds; anger destroys a gift; therefore self-control is above giving.
Unseen, great king, are ten thousand places in heaven, of the sages, in all worlds, from which gods go.
By self-control the great sages, lord of men, go to the great place they desire; therefore self-control is above giving.
A teacher gains imperishable fruit through hardship; having duly offered in the fire, he reaches Brahma's world, king.
One who, having studied the Vedas, gives them to those who know the law, and praises the work of the teacher, is honoured in heaven.
A kshatriya devoted to study, sacrifice and giving, and who protects in battle, is honoured in heaven.
A vaishya devoted to his own work gains much by giving; a shudra devoted to his own work gains heaven by service.
Heroes are said to be of many kinds; hear from me their purposes; the fruit for the lines of heroes and for the hero is told.
Men are said to be heroes of sacrifice, heroes of self-control, heroes of truth, heroes of battle and heroes of giving.
Others are heroes of understanding, others heroes of forgiveness, and men live as heroes of honesty and heroes of peace.
By those and those restraints many other heroes exist: heroes of Vedic study, heroes devoted to teaching,
heroes of serving the teacher, others of serving the father, heroes of serving the mother, others heroes of begging alms.
Many are heroes of Sankhya, others heroes of yoga, heroes of the forest and of household life, heroes of honouring guests; all go to the higher worlds won by the fruit of their own deeds.
Bearing all the Vedas, bathing in all sacred fords, and always speaking truth may or may not be equal.
A thousand horse sacrifices and truth were weighed on a scale; truth alone is distinguished above a thousand horse sacrifices.
By truth the sun burns, by truth fire blazes, by truth the wind blows; everything is established in truth.
By truth one pleases gods, ancestors and brahmanas; they call truth the highest dharma; therefore one should not transgress truth.
Sages are devoted to truth, sages are valiant in truth, sages swear by truth; therefore truth is distinguished; those with truth rejoice in the world of heaven, bull of the Bharatas.
Self-control, the gaining of the fruit of truth, has been told by me fully; undoubtedly everyone of trained self is honoured in heaven.
Hear, lord of the earth, the qualities of celibacy: one who is a celibate student from birth to death has nothing unattainable, know, lord of men.
Many ten millions of sages dwell in Brahma's world, of those always devoted to truth, self-controlled and of upward semen.
Celibacy practised would burn all sins, king; especially for a brahmana, for a brahmana is called fire.
This is seen directly by you in ascetic brahmanas: Shakra fears a celibate who has been assaulted; that is the fruit of celibacy seen here in the sages.
Hear also from me the dharma in honouring mother and father: one who serves his father and never envies, nor his mother, without ego, and his teacher and instructor,
know, king, his fruit to be the highest place in heaven; and the self-possessed serving the teacher does not see hell.
[Bhishma said:] There is nothing higher than the gift of a cow, lord of the earth; a cow justly obtained and given carries a family across at once.
One who is rightly produced for the good, who is rightly prepared and properly offered for subjects; therefore hear from me, king, the rule for the gift of cows, as it began in the first age.
Formerly, when cows had been brought, Mandhatri, seeing doubt, asked a question, and Brihaspati answered.
Having honoured a twice-born and told him the time for tomorrow, one of controlled vow should appoint Rohini for giving.
One should make the invocation "O Samanga, Bahula!" and, entering the midst of the cows, recite this verse:
The cow is my mother, the bull my father; heaven my refuge, earth my support. Having so taken refuge and spent the night among the cows, the sage should utter his speech in the gift of cows.
One equal in number and in vow to the cows for that one night, by oneness is freed from stain at once.
A cow with released bull and calf should be given at sunrise; three things are to be accepted: statements of meaning, blessings and praises.
So the giver of cows should first say half of it, as seen by rule before, and the twice-born receiving, knowing the rule, should answer the remaining half in the gift of cows.
I give a cow should be said, giving water, a garment and wealth; "To be filled with milk" and "of Vishnu" should be urged.
One should declare her name in order of number; the fruit is twenty-six and eight thousands and twenty.
Thus the giver of cows gains these increased qualities of cows and the rest in order, all of them in the eighth sequence.

A giver of cows is of good character, fearless, a giver of guest-water, not unhappy, a giver of wealth and desire-fulfilled; the one who bears the udder, Bharata, and the learned: the Vaishnava worlds are told.
Having given cows, one should be of the cow vow for three nights and spend one night with them here; one should live three nights on cow products, milk, dung or urine on the desired eighth.

The giver of a bull would be of the Vedic vow; the gift of a pair of oxen is the gaining of the Veda; so a sacrificer, reaching the rule of cows, gains the foremost worlds; one not knowing the rule does not.
One who gives a wish-granting cow, all earthly desires in one place: let those be rich in streams of offerings to gods and ancestors; and a gift of elder oxen.
One should not do favour to a non-pupil, one without vows, one without faith or one of crooked mind; this dharma of all the world is secret; one should not babble this dharma anywhere.
There are faithful men in the world; there are mean ones, rakshasas among men, to whom a gift being given is disliked, and the unmeritorious rely on non-belief.
Hearing this speech of Brihaspati, hear from me, king, of the kings who, having given cows, gained worlds, of meritorious character and good conduct.
Ushinara, Vishvagashva, Nriga, Bhagiratha the famed, Yuvanashva's son, Mandhatri, King Muchukunda, Bhuridyumna, the Naishadha and Somaka,
Pururavas, Bharata the emperor, in whose line all the Bharatas are, and the hero Rama son of Dasharatha, and others famed and glorious.
So King Dilipa, of wide deeds, knowing the rule, reached heaven by the gift of cows; Mandhatri was joined with sacrifices, gifts, austerity, kingly dharmas and gifts of cows.
Therefore, Partha, you too bear this Brihaspati's speech told by me; give it gladly to the best of the twice-born, cows, holy, having got the Kuru kingdom.
[Vaishampayana said:] Thus the king of dharma did everything, told by Bhishma, duly in the gift of cows; the king rightly bore the dharma taught by the god of gods to Mandhatri.
Thus, king, constantly in giving cows, drinking barley bits with dung, sleeping on the ground, tufted, self-restrained, he became then like a bull, a bull among kings.
That king became always pure of mind toward them, praising cows; and he never again yoked a cow at the yoke-pole, but went wherever with the best horses.
[Yudhishthira said:] Tell me again rightly the qualities in the gift of cows, Bharata; I am not satisfied, hero, hearing such nectar.
Thus addressed by the king of dharma, Shantanu's son then fully told him the sole fruits of the gift of cows.
[Bhishma said:] Giving such a cow to a brahmana, loving, rich in qualities, young and clothed, he is freed from all sins.
The worlds called Asurya are those to which he goes who gives a cow that has drunk water, eaten grass, lost her milk and senses,
for the old and fierce user, old like a waterless well; giving, he enters darkness and troubles the twice-born.
Vicious, angry, diseased or weak cows are not to be given; he who joins a brahmana with fruitless hardship of roots, his worlds are powerless and fruitless.
All praise those that are strong, rich in conduct and age, and fragrant; as the Ganga is the best of rivers, so the tawny is the best of the white cows.
[Yudhishthira said:] Why, in an equal gift, is the gift of a tawny cow praised by the good? I wish to hear the special reason, great-minded one; you are able to tell.
[Bhishma said:] Formerly Daksha, commanded by the Self-born "Create creatures," first created livelihood, wishing the good of beings.
As the dwellers of heaven live relying on nectar, so beings live relying on livelihood, lord.
Among beings, moving are better than unmoving, men better than these, and brahmanas better than those; in them sacrifices are established.
Soma is nourished by sacrifices, and he is established in cows; all the gods rejoice, and then subjects whose livelihood was before.
These beings cried out for livelihood, and thirsty went to the giver of livelihood as to father and mother.
Having thus gone in mind for the sake of creating creatures, the Prajapati then drank the nectar that gives strength.
Satisfied, breathing out a fragrant scent, he saw Surabhi, daughter born of his mouth, arisen from his belch.
Surabhi created the Saurabheyis, mothers of the world, gold-coloured tawny cows, the milch cows of livelihood for creatures.
From those nectar-coloured ones flowing on every side, foam born of nectar arose, like waves of rivers.
It fell from a calf's mouth on Bhava's head as he stood on earth; angry, the lord looked with the eye born of his forehead, as if burning the Rohinis.
That terrible splendour, lord of men, turned the tawny cows to various colours, as the sun the clouds.
Those that moved away from it and took refuge with Soma, standing in their own colour as they were born, were not led to another colour.
Then the Prajapati said to the angry Mahadeva: "You are sprinkled with nectar; there is no impurity in cows.
As Soma takes nectar and flows again, so these Rohinis, born of nectar, flow milk.
Wind is not defiled, nor fire, nor gold, nor the ocean; nectar drunk by nectar is not defiled, child; the drinkers were not children."
They will sustain these worlds with offerings and flow; take lordship of them, wholly made of nectar and auspicious.
The Prajapati gave him a bull along with them, and pleased Rudra's mind, Bharata.
Pleased, Mahadeva then made the bull his banner and his vehicle; therefore he is Bull-bannered.
Then the gods made Mahadeva lord of beasts; and in the midst of cows the lord is called Bull-marked.
Thus for the tawny cows of unfaded colour and great splendour, the first rule in giving is told for all of them.
Cows, eldest of the world, set going the world's livelihood, joined with Rudra, flows of Soma, gentle, holy, giving desires and giving life: giving cows, one would be a giver of all desires.
Reciting this excellent account of the origin of cows, always pure and fond of auspiciousness, a man is freed from the stain of the Kali age and gains dear sons and cattle wealth.
Offerings to gods and ancestors, satisfaction, rites of peace, vehicles, garments, and nourishment of old and young: all these qualities in the gift of cows the giver always gains, king.
[Vaishampayana said:] Hearing the grandfather's word, the king Partha with his brothers gave cows with gold and bronze milk-pails to the best of brahmanas.
So too he gave to those twice-born thousands and hundreds of cows, aiming at sacrifices and as fees, to win worlds and supreme fame.
[Narada said:] "Wearing the dress of a madman he wanders as he pleases, and constantly frequents the city of Varanasi."
The blessed one is our honoured one, the blessed one our teacher, the blessed one is the refuge of this kingdom and family.
Then Satrajiti Satya and Rukmini, O lord of men, running up, surrounded Dhananjaya and wept.
Karna's sons, mighty, and King Jayadratha, and Ghatotkacha and the others, and those not named.
